title: Freight broker software integration on Mac: how to fix system synchronization problems
metaTitle: Fix freight broker software integration issues on Mac
description: Learn why freight broker software integration fails and how to stop manual data entry on your Mac without expensive new systems.
intro: Freight broker software integration fails when your Transportation Management System refuses to talk to your email or accounting tools. This forces you to re-key data manually dozens of times every single day.
tldr: System synchronization is the primary cause of manual data entry in freight.
Legacy Windows software is the main barrier for Mac users.
You can fix data silos by moving to browser-based platforms.
Lazur helps by pointing to missing data and dictating entries for you.

blocks.text: Why freight broker software integration fails

Most freight brokerages grow by stacking tools. You add a load board, then a CRM, then an accounting platform. None of these tools were built to share data with each other. This creates data silos where information lives in your inbox instead of your TMS.

For Mac users, the problem is often worse. Many legacy TMS platforms were built for Windows. When you run them on a Mac using Parallels or Citrix, the connection is unstable. The software freezes, the data sync drops, and you end up manually verifying every single entry.
The hidden costs of manual data entry

Every time you copy a zip code from an email to your TMS, you risk a typo. These errors lead to incorrect rate confirmations and billing disputes. When you manage 15 to 25 email touchpoints per load, the margin for error is massive. You are essentially paying staff to act as human data relays.
How to fix synchronization without buying new software

items: Audit your current workflow to find where data is re-keyed.
Switch to web-based alternatives for your most used tools.
Use browser extensions to pull data directly into your TMS fields.
Standardize your email subject lines to help your team find documents faster.
Avoid using virtualization software like Parallels for your primary TMS.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to bridge the gap

Lazur does not click buttons for you, but it helps you move data faster. When you have a rate confirmation open in Chrome, you can hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur to extract the pickup date. You can then dictate that data directly into your TMS fields.

faq.question: Can I run legacy TMS on my Mac?
faq.answer: You can use Parallels, but it often causes sync issues. It is better to use a native browser-based TMS.

faq.question: Does Lazur integrate with my TMS?
faq.answer: Lazur is not a plugin. It is a voice assistant that sees your screen and helps you type faster.
